questions.stem: A menu has 4 entrees, 5 mains and 3 desserts. How many different three-course meals (one of each) can be chosen?
questions.explanation: By the multiplication principle, the choices multiply: 4 × 5 × 3 = 60. Adding them, 4 + 5 + 3 = 12, counts single dishes, not meals.

questions.stem: Evaluate 5!.
What is the value of 0!?
options: Undefined
questions.explanation: 0! is defined to be 1, so that formulas such as nPn = n!/0! = n! work. It counts the single way of arranging no objects.

questions.stem: Evaluate 8!/6!.
questions.explanation: 8!/6! = 8 × 7 × 6!/6! = 8 × 7 = 56. Cancelling to 8/6 treats the factorials as ordinary numbers.

questions.stem: In how many different orders can five candidates be listed on a ballot paper?
questions.explanation: There are 5 choices for first place, 4 for second, and so on: 5! = 120. The value 5⁵ = 3125 allows a candidate to be listed more than once.

questions.stem: Evaluate ⁷P₃, the number of arrangements of 3 objects chosen from 7.
questions.explanation: ⁷P₃ = 7 × 6 × 5 = 210. The value 35 is ⁷C₃, which ignores order, and 343 = 7³ allows repetition.

questions.stem: Which expression gives nPr, the number of permutations of r objects from n distinct objects?
options: n^r
n!/r!
questions.explanation: nPr = n(n − 1)...(n − r + 1) = n!/(n − r)!. Dividing also by r! gives the number of combinations, where order does not matter.

questions.stem: Number plates have 3 letters followed by 3 digits, and letters and digits may repeat. How many plates are possible?
questions.explanation: The multiplication principle gives 26 × 26 × 26 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 17 576 000. Not allowing repeats gives 11 232 000.

questions.stem: Number plates have 3 letters followed by 3 digits, with no letter or digit repeated. How many plates are possible?
questions.explanation: Without repetition there are 26 × 25 × 24 choices for the letters and 10 × 9 × 8 for the digits, giving 15 600 × 720 = 11 232 000. Allowing repeats gives 17 576 000.

questions.stem: How many arrangements of the letters of the word MATHS begin with M?
questions.explanation: With M fixed first, the other 4 letters can be arranged in 4! = 24 ways. The value 120 = 5! counts all arrangements, and 96 counts those that do not begin with M.

questions.stem: How many four-digit codes can be made from the digits 1 to 9, with no digit repeated, if the code must be even?
questions.explanation: The last digit must be 2, 4, 6 or 8 (4 choices); then the other places have 8, 7 and 6 choices: 4 × 8 × 7 × 6 = 1344. The value 3024 = ⁹P₄ ignores the even condition.

questions.stem: There are ⁵P₃ = 60 ordered arrangements of 3 students chosen from 5. How many unordered teams of 3 can be chosen?
questions.explanation: Each team of 3 can be arranged in 3! = 6 orders, so the number of teams is 60/6 = 10. This is how ⁵C₃ = ⁵P₃/3! links arrangements and selections.

questions.stem: At a meeting of 10 people, everyone shakes hands once with everyone else. How many handshakes are there?
questions.explanation: A handshake is an unordered pair, so the count is ¹⁰C₂ = (10 × 9)/2 = 45. Counting ordered pairs, 10 × 9 = 90, counts each handshake twice.

questions.stem: Six people stand in a row for a photo. In how many arrangements do two particular friends stand next to each other?
questions.explanation: Treat the friends as one unit: 5 units can be arranged in 5! = 120 ways, and the friends can swap places in 2 ways, giving 240. Forgetting the swap gives 120.

questions.stem: Which of these variables is continuous?
options: The mass of a bag of potatoes
The number of eggs in a carton
The number of teeth a person has
The number of cars in a car park
questions.explanation: Mass can take any value within a range, so it is continuous. The others are counts, which take only whole-number values and are discrete.

questions.stem: A student's height is measured with a ruler marked only in whole centimetres. Which statement is correct?
options: Height becomes discrete because the ruler shows whole centimetres
Height is discrete because it is a count of centimetres
Height is neither continuous nor discrete
Height is continuous, even though it is recorded as if discrete
questions.explanation: Height can take any value; a low-resolution instrument only makes the recorded values look discrete. The variable itself stays continuous.

questions.stem: Find the mean, median and mode of the data 3, 7, 7, 8, 10, 13.
options: Mean 8, median 7.5, mode 13
Mean 8, median 7.5, mode 7
Mean 7.5, median 8, mode 7
Mean 8, median 7, mode 7
questions.explanation: The mean is 48/6 = 8. With six values the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th, (7 + 8)/2 = 7.5. The mode, 7, occurs most often.

questions.stem: The annual salaries at a small business are mostly between $55 000 and $70 000, but the owner earns $400 000. Which measure best describes a typical salary?
options: The mode, because it is always the middle value
The median, because it is not affected by the extreme value
The mean, because it uses every salary
The range, because it shows the spread
questions.explanation: The single very large salary pulls the mean upwards, but the median depends only on the middle values. The range measures spread, not a typical value.

questions.stem: Using the median of each half, find the range and interquartile range of 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 15.
options: Range 6.5, IQR 13
Range 13, IQR 6.5
Range 13, IQR 6
Range 15, IQR 6.5
questions.explanation: The range is 15 − 2 = 13. The lower half 2, 4, 5, 7 has median Q1 = 4.5 and the upper half 8, 10, 12, 15 has Q3 = 11, so the IQR is 11 − 4.5 = 6.5.

questions.stem: Using s = √(Σ(x − x̄)²/(n − 1)), find the sample standard deviation of 2, 4, 4, 6, to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The mean is 4, and the squared deviations are 4, 0, 0 and 4, totalling 8. Then s = √(8/3) ≈ 1.63. Dividing by n = 4 gives √2 ≈ 1.41, and 2.67 is s², before the square root.

questions.stem: Find the sample standard deviation of 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The mean is 9; the squared deviations 16, 4, 0, 4, 16 total 40. Then s = √(40/4) = √10 ≈ 3.16. Dividing by 5 gives √8 ≈ 2.83, and 10 is the variance.

questions.stem: The masses of some parcels are measured in kilograms. In what units is their standard deviation?
options: Kilograms per parcel
Kilograms
Square kilograms
It has no units
questions.explanation: The standard deviation is the square root of an average squared deviation, so it has the same units as the data. Square kilograms are the units of the variance.

questions.stem: Every value in a data set is increased by 10. What happens to the mean and the standard deviation?
options: The mean increases by 10; the standard deviation is unchanged
Both increase by 10
The mean is unchanged; the standard deviation increases by 10
The mean increases by 10; the standard deviation increases by √10
questions.explanation: Adding 10 shifts every value and the centre by 10, but the distances from the mean stay the same, so the spread is unchanged.

questions.stem: Set P is 10, 10, 10, 10, 10 and set Q is 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. Which statement is correct?
options: Q has the larger mean and standard deviation
P has the larger standard deviation
Both have mean 10; Q has the larger standard deviation
Both have mean 10 and the same standard deviation
questions.explanation: Both sets have mean 10, but every value of P equals the mean, so its standard deviation is 0. The values of Q spread out from 10, so its standard deviation is positive.

questions.stem: Why is the interquartile range often preferred to the range for describing spread?
options: It has different units from the data
It is not affected by a few extreme values
It uses every value in the data
It is always larger than the range
questions.explanation: The IQR covers the middle 50% of the data, so one unusually large or small value barely changes it. The range depends only on the two most extreme values.

questions.stem: Which description is true of any normal distribution, whatever its mean and standard deviation?
options: It is skewed, with a long tail to the right
Its mean is always greater than its median
It is flat across its whole range
It is bell-shaped and symmetric about its mean
questions.explanation: A normal distribution is bell-shaped and symmetric, so its mean, median and mode coincide at the centre. A long tail to one side describes a skewed distribution.

questions.stem: Adult heights are approximately normally distributed. About what percentage of heights lie within one standard deviation of the mean?
questions.explanation: About 68% lie within one standard deviation, 95% within two and 99.7% within three. 50% lie on each side of the mean.

questions.stem: Why are many quantities, such as the volume of a can of soft drink, approximately normally distributed?
options: Every possible volume is equally likely
The volumes are counted, so they are discrete
Each value is the combined effect of many small random errors
The machine always fills to exactly the same volume
questions.explanation: When many small, independent random effects add together, the result tends to have a bell-shaped distribution. Equal likelihood for every volume would give a flat distribution instead.

questions.stem: Cans hold volumes that are normally distributed with mean 375 mL and standard deviation 3 mL. About what percentage of cans hold between 369 mL and 381 mL?
questions.explanation: 369 and 381 are each 6 mL, or two standard deviations, from the mean, and about 95% of values lie within two standard deviations. 47.5% is only the half from 375 to 381.

questions.stem: Battery lifetimes are normally distributed with mean 40 hours and standard deviation 5 hours. About what percentage last more than 50 hours?
questions.explanation: 50 hours is two standard deviations above the mean. About 95% lie within two standard deviations, leaving 5% in the two tails, so 2.5% lie above 50. Taking all 5% forgets that half of it is in the lower tail.

questions.stem: Battery lifetimes are normally distributed with mean 40 hours and standard deviation 5 hours. About what percentage last between 35 and 50 hours?
questions.explanation: From 35 to 40 is one standard deviation below the mean (34%), and from 40 to 50 is two above (47.5%), so the total is 81.5%. The interval is not symmetric, so neither 68% nor 95% applies.

questions.stem: A machine fills 1000 bags of rice with masses normally distributed, with mean 1.02 kg and standard deviation 0.01 kg. About how many bags weigh less than 1.00 kg?
questions.explanation: 1.00 kg is two standard deviations below the mean, so about 2.5% of bags are lighter: 2.5% of 1000 = 25. Using all 5% outside two standard deviations gives 50.

questions.stem: For a normal distribution, about what percentage of values are more than three standard deviations above the mean?
questions.explanation: About 99.7% lie within three standard deviations, leaving 0.3% split equally between the two tails, so 0.15% lie above. The value 0.3% counts both tails.

questions.stem: What is special about the points one standard deviation either side of the mean on a normal curve?
options: Half of all values lie between them
The curve changes from concave down to concave up there
The curve reaches its maximum height there
The curve meets the horizontal axis there
questions.explanation: At one standard deviation from the mean the bell curve changes the way it bends, from curving down near the peak to curving up in the tails. About 68%, not half, lies between these points.

questions.stem: In a normally distributed set of test scores, about 16% of scores are above 72 and about 16% are below 48. What are the mean and standard deviation?
options: Mean 60, standard deviation 6
Mean 50, standard deviation 12
Mean 60, standard deviation 12
Mean 60, standard deviation 24
questions.explanation: The symmetry puts the mean midway, at 60. About 68% lie between 48 and 72, so these are one standard deviation either side: 72 − 60 = 12. The width 24 spans two standard deviations.

questions.stem: A normal distribution has mean 60 and standard deviation 12. What value lies two standard deviations below the mean?
questions.explanation: Two standard deviations is 2 × 12 = 24, and 60 − 24 = 36. The value 48 is only one standard deviation below, and 24 is the distance, not the value.
